items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: He heard us and he came over and said, well, 'I'd like to get three of you... to come over and join our Minstrel Show.' ... He gave us $15.00 a week and a stateroom on the train.

ctx.x: And in Iowa City, a fellow There was they had another carnival which was playing in the next town from us called Isler Greater Shows, I-s-l-e-r, Greater, G-r-e-a-t-e-r Shows. Most people get that wrong. They call it the Gravy Show, but it's Greater.

The and this fellow that ran the Minstrel Show was named Rasus Jones (PROMOTER). and He heard us and he came over and said, well, "I'd like to get three of you, the trumpet player and the saxophone, you, Eddie, and the piano player to come over and join our Minstrel Show." Well, we were kids; we didn't know how to go about it. So in the middle of the night we sneaked off from the show and went over to the other. We were getting $10.00 a week in this first show. Well, He gave us $15.00 a week and a stateroom on…

Well, we traveled all through Iowa and then we went down into Kansas, and we went to -- in fact, when we were in Leavenworth, Kansas I met George Lee who was a band out of orchestra and Kansas City and he was with his sister, Julia Lee. And I went out that night and set in with them. Then I met a fellow in the Army whose name was Sawyer. And He wanted me to join the Army Sawyer was a saxophone player in the Army band. And, you know, I was a jazz man. I didn't know how to play anything else.
